correctness.rationale: For any edge sequence, the sum of the k smallest opinions is monotone and the square-energy identity makes per-step jumps vanish, forcing each labeled opinion to converge. Uniformly positive conditional sampling proves by geometric avoidance that infinite receptivity entails infinite selected receptive meetings. Edges with different endpoint limits cannot meet receptively infinitely often; with equal endpoint limits one sufficiently late receptive meeting raises confidence at least gamma and locks in all subsequent receptivity. These exhaustive cases and finiteness of E prove whole-network fixation. When delta<1, repeated selections force each permanently present confidence to 1 and each absent confidence to 0; the endpoint delta=1 is properly exempt from this latter equivalence.

originality.rationale: The 2025 full primary article explicitly leaves eventual constancy of its asynchronous adaptive-confidence effective graph unresolved; existing theorems address opinion convergence, confidence limits, and a weaker edge-endpoint condition. Full-text/model comparisons plus mathematical-result searches identify no stronger covering result. Conditional Borel–Cantelli and doubly stochastic averaging are classical; only their precise combination with permanently increasing selected-edge confidence is the new claim. Residual publication-priority risk persists.

value.rationale: Resolves the precise graph-constancy question explicitly left open for the finite asynchronous adaptive-confidence DW model in the published 2025 source. Distinguishes graph locking from mere convergence of agent opinions, covers arbitrary finite networks and all delta endpoints, and yields a substantive persistent-sampling robustness theorem; not merely a numerical or normalization check.
